description: UK population calibration contract: value-free national and local-geography target declarations over Chronicle facts. Selection contracts live in Microcosm per the chronicle#166 ruling (2026-08-13): Chronicle is a facts-only layer; Microcosm owns which facts are targets and how they bind to the model. This resource consolidates the former national and local-geography contracts into one population contract while preserving both target levels and their provenance accounting blocks. Observed values resolve from hash-pinned Chronicle consumer-facts artifacts at build time.

The four deleted universal-credit jobseeker dispatch names were not registry rows in the carried contract, so there were no parity entries to remove; obr/jobseekers_allowance remains a distinct published JSA expenditure target.
accounting_notes.cross_level_duplicate_names: Name-only identity flattens two-level emissions for ons/uk_population, ons/scotland_children_under_16, and ons/scotland_babies_under_1.
accounting_notes.salary_sacrifice_obr_near_equivalents: The contract separately maps OBR near-equivalents obr/salary_sacrifice_employee_ni_relief and obr/salary_sacrifice_employer_ni_relief onto hmrc.salary_sacrifice.nics_relief_employee and hmrc.salary_sacrifice.nics_relief_employer.
accounting_notes.two_child_limit_year_surface: Chronicle's 15 dwp/uc/two_child_limit/* facts are the April-2025 publication (period month 2025-04) and are the only TCL facts; there are no 2026 Ledger facts. At 12a1e028, the incumbent pins the same published numbers at {2026}, so at calibration year 2025 Ledger activates all 15 TCL targets while the incumbent drops them from the 652-row union to the 637-row effective surface; the 2026 effective surface remains 652. The same 12a1e028 refresh adds the new incumbent dwp/uc/households row. Fixture B treats the 15 TCL rows as enumerated ledger-side additions.
accounting_notes.geography_level_order_canonicalization: The 9 voa.council_tax_stock.* rows use country, region order to match the rest of the contract; consumers use membership only.
accounting_notes.ons_terminal_sex_band_split: María ruling 2026-08-21: split the incumbent terminal sex bands into uniform five-year 85_89 bands plus 90_plus tails. The incumbent six-year 85_90 terminal rows leave ages 91+ unconstrained; Microcosm keeps the uniform five-year bands and constrains the tail. The 85_89-vs-85_90 value gap is the single-age-90 share and is a signed semantic difference.

Mean monthly paid GB benefit units over the exact twelve months of calendar 2025. Use the publisher Child Entitlement Total within each child-count/payment category, not the sum of perturbed Yes/No detail cells; no child-entitlement filter is added to the model. Benefit-unit count among positive UC awards. Child counts use retained FRS child members under 20 and UC child/qualifying-young-person status, excluding claimant/parent roles. DWP reported children can exceed those eligible for a child element. Benefit-unit grain retains the microcosm#809 correction for multibenunit households. Simulated entitlement is unchanged. Count only the Great Britain regions, matching K03000001; DWP removes Northern Ireland-office claims from these statistics. Mean monthly paid GB benefit units over the exact twelve months of calendar 2025. Count each Scottish UC benefit unit with its own reported child under one; a baby or UC claim in a different benefit unit in the same dwelling does not qualify it. Source April–December 2025 mean covers nine observations. Annual positive model UC remains a proxy for the source claim/payment state.

Count UC benefit units and their own dependent children/qualifying young people, excluding claimant/partner roles. Statistical affected children are third or subsequent own qualifying children born on/after the source cutoff, including exceptions; this is separate from losing a child element. The current measurement is explicitly a proxy: annual universal_credit > 0 for source open claims, and model birth_year >= 2017 for 6 April 2017. Retain the source April observation date; annual assignment does not create a yearly average or an April claim-history replay. Claimant PIP counts only retained claimant/partner roles; disabled-child-element status counts only own qualifying children. GB residential-region mask excludes NI. Source: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/universal-credit-claimants-statistics-on-the-two-child-limit-policy-april-2025/background-information-and-methodology
